title: PCAOB Release No. 2018-006: Amendments to Auditing Standards for Auditor's Use of the Work of Specialists (incl. Appendix 1 rule text of AS 1210, Using the Work of an Auditor-Engaged Specialist, and AS 1105 Appendix A)
data_collection_dates: Inspection data analyses cited in release: 2015 and 2017 inspection cycles
limitations: Access route: pcaobus.org standard page returned HTTP 403 to both curl and WebFetch; the 149-page adopting release PDF was retrieved from the alternate PCAOB domain pcaob.org (Docket 044). Rule text is as ADOPTED on 2018-12-20 (SEC-approved 2019-07-01, Release 34-86270; effective for audits of fiscal years ending on or after 2020-12-15). The PCAOB lists later conforming amendments to AS 1210 (e.g., PCAOB Release 2022-002), which were not checked; current codified text may differ in minor wording. A standard shows an obligation, not compliance, cost, or demand. Inspection statistics come from risk-selected (non-random) engagements, as the release itself notes.

title: Public Company Accounting Oversight Board; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rules on Amendments to Auditing Standards for Auditor's Use of the Work of Specialists (84 FR 13442, Release No. 34-85435, File No. PCAOB-2019-01)
authors_or_organization: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Federal Register (filing by PCAOB)
limitations: Same underlying rulemaking as WS7-S01 (not independent evidence). Used to record the SEC/Federal Register access route and the Board's own summary of the risk-based scaling intent. The SEC approval order PDF (Release 34-86270) on sec.gov returned a 'Request Rate Threshold Exceeded' page to curl and was not read.

title: Does the Whole Exceed its Parts? The Effect of AI Explanations on Complementary Team Performance (CHI '21)
authors_or_organization: Gagan Bansal, Tongshuang Wu, Joyce Zhou, Raymond Fok, Besmira Nushi, Ece Kamar, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Daniel S. Weld (University of Washington; Microsoft Research; Allen Institute for AI)
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Co-authors affiliated with Microsoft Research; acknowledgements/funding not extracted
limitations: Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers (US, >=97% approval); low-stakes common-sense tasks (sentiment of beer/book reviews, LSAT logic questions); AI accuracy deliberately matched to human accuracy (84% sentiment; 65% LSAT); small per-task payments with accuracy bonuses; outcome is decision accuracy only (no time or effort measured objectively); explanations are AI saliency highlights or expert-written narratives, not citations to source evidence. Not an advisor-client structure. Authors state results may not generalize to high-stakes expert domains.

title: To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making (Proc. ACM HCI 5, CSCW1, Article 188)
authors_or_organization: Zana Buçinca, Maja Barbara Malaya, Krzysztof Z. Gajos (Harvard University; Lodz University of Technology)
limitations: MTurk lay participants (N=199 analysed of 260 recruited), single non-critical nutrition task chosen because experts are costly to recruit; simulated AI with designed errors (6 of 24 scored trials incorrect); within-subject two-block design with exploratory conditions excluded; no objective time/effort measure reported; explanations are feature-based (carb/flavor estimates), not provenance. Not an advisor-client structure.

title: Lawyering in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (109 Minn. L. Rev. 147 (2024)) - repository landing page and abstract
authors_or_organization: Jonathan H. Choi, Amy B. Monahan, Daniel Schwarcz
data_collection_dates: not reported in accessed material (SSRN version posted 2023-11-09)
limitations: Full text NOT reviewed: PDF links at scholarship.law.umn.edu (viewcontent.cgi), minnesotalawreview.org, and SSRN all returned Cloudflare bot challenges/403 to curl and WebFetch; not bypassed. Only the published abstract was read. Law-review article (student-edited, not peer-reviewed in the scientific sense). Participants were law students, not practicing lawyers; tasks were drafting/analysis tasks, not review of an outside advisor's work.

title: Lawyering in the Age of Artificial Intelligence - SSRN abstract as reproduced on TaxProf Blog (2023-11-16)
authors_or_organization: TaxProf Blog (AALS) reproducing abstract by Choi, Monahan & Schwarcz
limitations: Secondary reproduction of the 2023 SSRN-version abstract; retrieved via WebFetch (model-summarized output), so wording was not independently verified character-by-character; used only for design facts (N=60 students, four tasks, training on GPT-4).

title: AI helps lawyers complete work quicker, study finds (Legal Futures)
limitations: News coverage of the same study; retrieved via WebFetch summarizer; the reported 12%-32% time-saving range could not be checked against the paper's tables because full text was blocked.

title: Towards a Science of Human-AI Decision Making: A Survey of Empirical Studies (arXiv:2112.11471v1; later published as 'Towards a Science of Human-AI Decision Making: An Overview of Design Space in Empirical Human-Subject Studies', FAccT 2023)
authors_or_organization: Vivian Lai, Chacha Chen, Q. Vera Liao, Alison Smith-Renner, Chenhao Tan
data_collection_dates: Literature surveyed: >100 empirical human-subject papers (venues incl. CHI, CSCW, IUI, FAccT, NeurIPS etc.) up to 2021
funding_or_commercial_relationships: Co-author affiliations include Microsoft Research and Dataminr
limitations: The full text read is the 2021 arXiv survey version, not the FAccT 2023 camera-ready; counts and wording may differ in the published version. Narrative/coded survey without pooled effect sizes; does not quantify the share of studies with expert participants in the passages extracted.

title: Appropriate Reliance on AI Advice: Conceptualization and the Effect of Explanations (IUI '23; arXiv:2302.02187v3)
authors_or_organization: Max Schemmer, Niklas Kühl, Carina Benz, Andrea Bartos, Gerhard Satzger (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology)
limitations: Prolific crowdworkers (N=200; one excluded); deceptive hotel-review task on which humans perform near chance; AI down-sampled to 50% accuracy on the 16 main items (4 per confusion-matrix cell); feature-importance highlights, not provenance; no time/effort measure in extracted results.

title: Automation bias: a systematic review of frequency, effect mediators, and mitigators (J Am Med Inform Assoc 2012;19(1):121-127)
authors_or_organization: Kate Goddard, Abdul Roudsari, Jeremy C. Wyatt
data_collection_dates: Database searches retrieving 13,821 papers (after de-duplication); 74 included
limitations: Mixed fields (healthcare, aviation, generic); pooled meta-analysis is small and 'indicative' (4 healthcare CDSS studies). Mediator findings (experience, accountability) are vote-counted narrative syntheses, several from aviation/student samples. Pre-dates generative AI. Decision support systems are tools, not outside advisors.

title: Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance on AI Systems During Decision-Making (Proc. ACM HCI 7, CSCW1, Article 129; arXiv:2212.06823v2)
authors_or_organization: Helena Vasconcelos, Matthew Jörke, Madeleine Grunde-McLaughlin, Tobias Gerstenberg, Michael S. Bernstein, Ranjay Krishna (Stanford; University of Washington)
limitations: Prolific crowdworkers; artificial maze-solving task where verification of a highlighted path is visually easy; simulated AI; 5 studies N=731 total (Study 2 reuses Study 1 highlight-condition data). Bayesian model estimates reported on model scale (specification in appendix, not extracted). Task has an unambiguous ground truth, unlike most diligence judgments.

title: In Search of Verifiability: Explanations Rarely Enable Complementary Performance in AI-Advised Decision Making (arXiv:2305.07722v4; AI Magazine 2024)
limitations: Full text retrieved but only the abstract and introduction were reviewed in this timebox. Conceptual/theory synthesis of prior experiments, not new data.

title: Proxy Tasks and Subjective Measures Can Be Misleading in Evaluating Explainable AI Systems (IUI '20; arXiv:2001.08298)
authors_or_organization: Zana Buçinca, Phoebe Lin, Krzysztof Z. Gajos, Elena L. Glassman (Harvard University)
limitations: Full text retrieved; only the abstract was reviewed in this timebox, so sample sizes and effect sizes are not recorded. Lay online participants plus an in-person think-aloud study.

title: RSNA press release: AI Bias May Impair Radiologist Accuracy on Mammogram (on Dratsch et al., 'Automation Bias in Mammography: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence BI-RADS Suggestions on Reader Performance', Radiology 2023, doi:10.1148/radiol.222176)
authors_or_organization: Radiological Society of North America (press release on study by Thomas Dratsch et al.)
limitations: Press release only; the Radiology article and PubMed abstract were not read (PubMed returned a cookie/bot page). Moderately experienced group results and statistical tests not available from the release. Simulated ('purported') AI with deliberately incorrect suggestions on 12 of 40 cases; reader-study setting, not clinical practice.

title: Man Versus Machine: Complex Estimates and Auditor Reliance on Artificial Intelligence (Journal of Accounting Research 60(1):171-201) - repository abstract
authors_or_organization: Benjamin P. Commerford, Sean A. Dennis, Jennifer R. Joe, Jenny W. Ulla
limitations: Abstract only (UNLV repository landing page); participant count, experience level, effect sizes and design details not reviewed. Experimental case, not field audits.
